en: The Octave on Kālabhairava
I bow to the one whose pure lotus feet are served by the king of the gods, who wears a serpent as his sacrificial thread, who has the moon as his crest-jewel, who is compassionate,
who is saluted by hosts of yogis such as Nārada, and who is clothed only by the directions.
I worship Kālabhairava, the lord of the city of Kāśī—
the supreme blue-throated one with three eyes, who shines like ten million suns, who delivers beings from the ocean of existence, and who bestows all desired objects.
...the lotus-eyed one who is death unto death, the imperishable one whose weapon is the trident; Kāśikā [worships] the primordial cause,
the dark-bodied primordial deity, the imperishable and free from affliction, who holds in his hands the trident, the axe, the noose, and the staff.
Kāśikā [worships] the Lord of terrible prowess, who delights in the wonderful tāṇḍava dance,
the bestower of worldly enjoyment and liberation, and whose beautiful form is highly praised.
To Him who is affectionate toward His devotees, who stands as the embodiment of all the worlds,
whose waist shines with beautiful golden bells tinkling melodiously— [this is] the first part of the *Bṛhatstotraratnākara*.
The Kāśikā...
[praises] the All-pervading Lord, the protector of the bridge of Dharma, the destroyer of the path of unrighteousness, the liberator from the bonds of karma, and the bestower of true happiness.
Her body’s orb is adorned with the remaining golden-colored noose;
her pair of feet is made beautiful by the luster of jeweled sandals— she who is eternally peerless, the beloved deity, and stainless.
Kāśikā is the destroyer of the mirror of death, the liberator from terrible fangs,
[and] the shatterer of the continuous series of the lotus-egg of Brahmā by her loud laughter;
she is the one who casts away the web of sins with a mere glance and the fierce punisher of evil-doers.
Wearing a garland of skulls that bestows the eight supernatural powers,
[he is] the leader of the assembly of spirits and the giver of vast renown.
...the all-pervading Lord, the ancient Master of the World, who dwells in Kāśī, who purifies the merit and demerit of the world, and who is skilled in the path of ethics— [Kośikā... 8.
Those who recite this captivating *Kālabhairavāṣṭaka*— the means for attaining knowledge and liberation, which increases manifold merit— [attain the highest goal].
They certainly go into the presence of the feet of Kālabhairava, which destroy grief, delusion, wretchedness, greed, anger, and torment.
Thus [ends the chapter] of the venerable Paramahaṃsa Parivrājaka Ācārya...
In the work of the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda,
the Kālabhairavāṣṭaka is complete.
